text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: GPU allocation failures (cuda::alloc) in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Auto-page policy: P1 -> on-call. Logs attached.

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-serving-gpu, incident=INC-48271. Escalation: primary on-call -> alex.

alex: Acked on PagerDuty. Looking now. Which pools are affected?

tess: seeing alloc failures on pool=gpu-pool-48 (us-west-2) and gpu-pool-12 (eu-central-1). Error snippet: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 1.2 GiB` repeated across tens of tasks.

sam: Confirmed increased kvcache evictions prior to failures, also a surge of long-context generations hitting 32k sequences. Could be fragmentation + large kv spikes.

carla: Any customer impact observed? Monitoring shows 2% 5xxs on /v1/generate in us-west-2 and 6% tail latency > 5s for embeddings in eu-central-1. Some requests auto-fell back to smaller model variant.

alex: Good to know. First mitigation: drain incoming traffic from affected pools to fallback pools and enable model fallback for the next 10m. I'm running the drain script now.

alex: Run: ```./infra/drain_pool.sh --pool gpu-pool-48 --reason "OOM surge" --timeout 600```

tess: Drain started for gpu-pool-48. Putting routing rule to divert new sessions to fallback-pool-usw2. Patching route in nginx-router (canary 10%).

sam: For eu-central-1 I see a few noisy customers sending long streaming requests. Suggest we throttle max sequence length for new sessions until we stabilize. Can set a soft limit at the gateway.

carla: Noting impacted customers: customer:acme-marketing (some embed requests delayed), customer:finlytics (has high concurrency but on dedicated capacity; no impact), customer:chatly (fallback to cheaper model, degraded quality). Recording for postmortem.

alex: Temporary config changes: 1) route 100% of new /v1/generate to fallback pools for us-west-2; 2) set max_sequence_length=16384 for new sessions in eu-central-1; 3) increase eviction aggressiveness on kvcache. Applying now.

tess: Applied k8s rollout for router config and updated seq limit via feature flag. Monitoring.

sam: I patched the kvcache memory threshold to 0.7 (was 0.9) on both pools to force earlier evictions; also triggered a forced GC on the runtime for the top 3 nodes.

incident-bot: Noted actions: route-change, seq-limit, kvcache-threshold-change. Auto-pager still unack window expired -> no further escalation.

carla: After routing changes, error rate dropped to 0.3% in us-west-2 and latency normalized in eu-central-1 to baseline. Some degraded-quality reports from chatly but functional.

alex: Will keep pools drained for 15m then gradually reintroduce. Need to investigate root cause: likely sequence-length surge causing fragmentation and eviction storm. Plan: capture heap+nvml snapshots from affected nodes and collect kernel logs.

sam: Capturing nvml snapshots now: saving to s3://redwood-debug/INC-48271/usw2/ and .../euc1/. Also dumping kvcache metrics and recent allocations.

tess: Assigning follow-ups: (1) infra/serving to analyze fragmentation (sam), (2) runtime to add defensive fallback when kv eviction rate spikes (alex), (3) outreach to customers (carla).

carla: I notified account reps for acme-marketing and chatly with a short incident note and ETA for a full postmortem within 48h.

alex: Handoff to night on-call (sam) in 30m. I'll leave the drain in place and a rollback plan in #eng-runtime in case routers misbehave.

sam: I have the pager on. If we see repeat OOMs after reintroducing traffic, next step is to temporarily restrict max concurrent requests per org.

incident-bot: Incident tagged as "investigate:gpu-alloc-surge" and severity P1 -> reduced to P2 after stabilization.

carla: Closing notes: brief summary appended to incident tracker INC-48271. Will attach logs and timelines. Postmortem owners assigned.

alex: Thanks everyone. If anything flares up ping me directly. :thumbsup:
